title: Procurement-context-gradient (E2) DecisionContext + per-field provenance
description: Forked from procurement-decisions/runner/contracts/decision_context.schema.json at SHA 10f5475d9efa8c4682ac73b6956e3aeb46854e70. E2 extends the canonical fields with a single new audit-only-but-hash-bound key: `governance_context_level`. The eval-loop / multi-pass orchestrator injects this field (alongside the existing `agent_*` audit fields) before posting to MeshQu, so the level marker rides into the integrity hash via the API's existing canonical-json envelope — no @meshqu/core change required. Policy rules continue to read only the substantive substrate-derived fields; `governance_context_level` is invisible to evaluation but cryptographically attested in every receipt.

DecisionContext.description: Payload passed to MeshQu /v1/decisions/record. `context.fields` carries the flat policy-evaluable field set; `context.metadata` carries operational annotations that the receipt's integrity hash deliberately excludes (per the 2026-05-14 codebase-audit corrections in planning/decision_log.md — only `fields` is hashed, `metadata` is stripped before hashing).

decision_type.description: Locked to `procurement_decision` for the experiment. Selects which policies in the experiment-procurement tenant evaluate this record.

fields.description: Flat field set sent to MeshQu and bound into the receipt's integrity hash. Two producers contribute keys: (a) the **substrate adapter** emits the substantive policy-evaluable fields below (the ratified policy's 6 rules only read these); (b) the **eval loop** injects the `agent_*` audit-only fields after the agent call returns and before posting to MeshQu. Both groups live in the same map so they bind into one integrity hash. The policy never evaluates `agent_*` keys — they're hash-bound metadata only. Booleans MUST be the strings 'true'/'false' to match the policy's when-clause authoring (decision_log F13 cross-over finding); flipping to JSON booleans silently breaks rule firing.

publication_delay_days.description: PROC-001-S53. (awards[0].datePublished − awards[0].date) in days. Award date is the substrate proxy for contract signature date.

above_threshold.description: PROC-001-S53, PROC-005 when. Proxy: tender.value.amount (or awards[0].value.amount fallback) > £139,000 (PA23 Schedule 1 sub-central services threshold).

supplier_id.description: PROC-003. awards[0].suppliers[0].id (canonicalised: trimmed, original casing preserved).

conflict_of_interest_declaration.description: PROC-004 (COI declaration). NOT IN OCDS — omitted by the substrate. PROC-004 is gated by a `when` clause requiring this field to be present (`{ field: 'conflict_of_interest_declaration', exists: true }`), so absence skips the rule rather than triggering it (NA-reason: 'conflict of interest declaration is missing'). A future substrate variant that derives COI from a richer source will cause PROC-004 to evaluate. The `when`-clause gate was applied 2026-05-17 after the 3-record smoke surfaced that the prior wiring fired PROC-004 on absence — see planning/decision_log.md 'Post-smoke policy clarification' entry.

procurement_method_open_flag.description: PROC-005 (presence). Emitted as the string 'true' when tender.procurementMethod == 'open'. Omitted when procurement method is anything else — the presence rule fires when the flag is absent + the when clause matches.

direct_award_justification_present.description: PROC-005 when. Heuristic: derived from relatedProcesses tagged 'transparency' or 'directAward'. False-negatives possible where the notice exists but isn't linked.

is_modification.description: PROC-006 when. Derived from OCDS tag (contractAmendment / awardAmendment / modification).

modification_value_ratio.description: PROC-006. (amendments[0].value.amount / original contract value). Only emitted when both numerator and denominator are derivable. NULL allowed when not a modification — see no-silent-defaults rule.

agent_model_id.description: AUDIT-ONLY (not evaluated). Locked model id (e.g. 'gpt-5.4-2026-03-05'). Injected by the eval loop after the agent call returns. Mirrors agent.LOCKED_MODEL_ID.

agent_model_version.description: AUDIT-ONLY (not evaluated). Reserved for the rare case where OpenAI's response surfaces a more specific version than the locked model id; null otherwise.

agent_temperature.description: AUDIT-ONLY (not evaluated). Locked temperature (0.0 in this experiment). Bound into the receipt so a reproducibility check can prove the agent ran at the declared temperature.

agent_prompt_sha256.description: AUDIT-ONLY (not evaluated). SHA-256 of the system prompt at run start. Computed once per run; identical across all records in a run.

agent_reasoning_sha256.description: AUDIT-ONLY (not evaluated). SHA-256 of the agent's reasoning text for THIS record (normalised: trim + LF). Full reasoning lives in the agent_outputs sidecar; only the hash is bound into the receipt.

agent_recommended_verdict.description: AUDIT-ONLY (not evaluated). The agent's normalised verdict for the agreement projection. The MeshQu policy verdict is computed independently from substrate fields; this field captures what the agent thought.

agent_recommended_action.description: AUDIT-ONLY (not evaluated). The agent's free-text recommended action (e.g. 'approve', 'escalate to counsel'). Null when the agent didn't produce one.

governance_context_level.description: E2 EXTENSION (v3). AUDIT-ONLY (not evaluated). The context-ladder level under which this record was evaluated. Injected by the multi-pass orchestrator BEFORE posting to MeshQu so the level marker is bound into the receipt's integrity hash via the existing canonical-JSON envelope. L0..L4 are the main grid (see planning/context_ladder_design.md); L4_PERMUTED is the adversarial diagnostic control (see planning/experiment_design.md §'Diagnostic Controls'). The policy never references this key — it rides along with the `agent_*` fields as audit-only-but-hash-bound metadata. Receipts from this experiment are cryptographically distinguishable from E1's by this field's presence alone (E1's policy_snapshot_id maps to the same snapshot, but no receipt under that policy can carry this field unless emitted by the E2 runner).

metadata.description: Operational annotations stripped from the receipt's integrity hash. Carries OCDS provenance + adapter version for the writeup's reproducibility statement.

ocid.description: OCDS Open Contracting ID for the source record. Strictly informational for the receipt; the writeup uses it to cross-reference back to Contracts Finder.

adapter_version.description: substrate.py's ADAPTER_VERSION at production time. Bumped on substantive derivation changes.

SubstrateProvenance.description: Per-field source + confidence metadata. Produced alongside the DecisionContext by the substrate adapter; logged into decision_traces.jsonl's substrate_notes for every record so the writeup can statistically analyse 'disagreement rate on direct fields vs disagreement rate on proxy-derived fields'. NOT sent to MeshQu — substrate-internal.

fields.description: One envelope per field that COULD be emitted (including absent ones). Keys match DecisionContext.fields keys.

FieldProvenance.description: Per-field provenance envelope. Same key set across every record (absent fields explicitly carry status='absent' so coverage statistics are computable).

value.description: The emitted value as it appears in DecisionContext.fields. Omitted for status='absent'. Type matches the field's DecisionContext schema.

status.description: Provenance class. direct_ocds = field copied verbatim from OCDS path. derived = computed from one or more OCDS fields with no methodological proxy (e.g. date arithmetic). proxy = computed using a documented methodological proxy (e.g. award date as signature date). absent = field not derivable from OCDS for this record (always honest — never a silent default).

confidence.description: Substrate confidence in the derivation, NOT model/agent confidence. high = direct OCDS path or trivial arithmetic. medium = proxy with documented limitations. low = heuristic with known false-negative or false-positive modes (e.g. derived_direct_award_justification_present).

detail.description: Human-readable explanation of the derivation step or absence reason. Quoted in the writeup's substrate-honesty subsection for the most interesting derivations.
